clue.text: Extremely cold place in which a Christian has a spasm

parts.note: RC, Roman Catholic, is a Christian
a tic is an involuntary muscular spasm

explanation.surface: Somewhere freezing where a believer suffers a sudden twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar region round the North Pole is the archetypal frozen spot on Earth.

clue.text: Show her drama?

parts.note: with the question mark, 'her' stands for some woman, here Di, so 'her' gives Di's
a play is a piece of drama

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a woman's stage work is worth putting on.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'her' must be read as a named woman: Di, the common crossword short form of Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit something is to put it on view, a synonym.

clue.text: Not quite true

parts.note: true can mean exactly aligned, as a wheel runs true; something slightly out of alignment is not quite true

explanation.definitionFit: Something slightly misaligned is displaced from its middle point, so not exactly straight.

clue.text: Alma knits with a French former female student

indicators.note: knitting works strands together into a new form, so these letters are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: A woman named Alma sits knitting with a Frenchwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knits' shuffles ALMA together with UN, the French for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman graduate of a school or college is one of its old girls, the feminine of alumnus.

clue.text: Displeasure about lake fish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for displeasure goes round the lake's letter

parts.note: anger is displeasure
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed about the fish in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The anglerfish is a sea creature that lures prey with a rod-like spine.

clue.text: Gun used in a brusque manner

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a different manner, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weapon is handled in a curt, abrupt way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manner' rearranges the letters of A BRUSQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An early portable firearm from the fifteenth century, fired from the shoulder.

clue.text: Hang about a west African country

indicators.note: about here means turned around or jumbled, so the four letters of the verb are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone is told to linger around a nation in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang' looks like the verb to linger, but it is the anagram fodder; 'about' is its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation on the Gulf of Guinea, once the Gold Coast.

clue.text: Biblical interpretation of the conversion of six geese

indicators.note: a conversion changes one thing into another, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A scholar reads scripture in the light of six birds being transformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion of' rearranges the letters of SIX GEESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Critical explanation of a text, especially scripture, is the theologian's word for interpretation.

clue.text: Shower with autumn precipitation

parts.note: a shower of water from the sky is rain
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Showers come along with the autumn weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount of water falling from clouds, measured as weather.

clue.text: Sorts out town centres!

definitions.meaning: to settle or put right, as in squaring a debt or a dispute
open plazas at the heart of towns

explanation.surface: Something organises the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: To square things is to settle them, and open public spaces form the hubs of many towns.

clue.text: Subject taken by highest international college, initially

parts.note: top means highest

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word college is used

explanation.surface: A leading international college takes on a field of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Take heed of daily letter writing material

parts.note: to note something is to take heed of it
a daily is a newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pay attention to the daily's correspondence supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery sheets used for correspondence.

clue.text: Bound to repay some of the borrowed money

indicators.note: some of signals that only part of the word borrowed is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A borrower is obliged to return part of a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' picks a run of letters from inside 'borrowed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in debt is to be obliged to pay back.

clue.text: Series of shops looked at a certain power tool

parts.note: a chain is a series of shops under one owner
saw means looked at

explanation.surface: A row of stores inspected a particular electric tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor-driven cutting device with teeth on a loop, a tool for felling trees.

clue.text: Ideal place is up to a1 standard

indicators.note: the letters are brought up to standard, put into proper order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the figure 1 looks like the letter I, so a1 reads as AI

explanation.surface: A perfect spot reaches the very highest grade.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the 1 in 'a1' as the letter I; 'standard' then rearranges UPTOAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's imaginary perfect state, now any perfect society.

clue.text: Will rewrite statement

indicators.note: to rewrite is to set the material out again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to redraft a declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will is a legal document disposing of property after death.

clue.text: Monster youth eats an Hellenic character

indicators.note: eats means takes in, so the word for youth surrounds the Greek letter

parts.note: a minor is a young person
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A fearsome creature: a youngster swallows a Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull-headed beast of the Cretan labyrinth in Greek myth.

clue.text: Desert sailor going westwards

indicators.note: in an across clue westwards is right to left, so the word for sailor is read backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman heads west across the sands.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is to abandon or betray them.

clue.text: International weapons rivalry in which members compete

parts.note: arms are limbs, members of the body
to race is to compete

explanation.surface: A global competition over weaponry where the participants are rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition between nations to build up military power, as in the Cold War.

clue.text: Utilise beginners' untapped, selfless enthusiasm

indicators.note: the beginners are the first letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to harness untapped, selfless zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginners'' takes the first letters of 'untapped, selfless, enthusiasm'.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ is to put into service, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Two small countries join to identify a guilty person

parts.note: small means abbreviated: FIN is the abbreviation for Finland and GER for Germany
small means abbreviated: FIN is the abbreviation for Finland and GER for Germany

explanation.surface: Two little nations unite to name the culprit.
explanation.definitionFit: To point the finger at someone is to accuse them, so the verb means to inform on.

clue.text: Start talking with internal dialect of 6

indicators.note: start means the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Someone begins speaking an inner language of a neighbouring land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' takes the first letters of 'talking with internal'. The 6 refers to 6-down, the West African country.
explanation.definitionFit: A language of the Akan people spoken widely in Ghana.

clue.text: Criticised the course going round the way point

indicators.note: going round means the road surrounds the following letters

parts.note: a road is a course or route
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone was slated for a route that loops past a waypoint.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them severely, slang.

clue.text: Usually as far as one can go to the left

definitions.text: Usually as far as one can go to the left

parts.words: Usually as far as one can go to the left
parts.note: on a conventional map the left edge is a compass direction, so the farthest left is usually the extreme in that direction

explanation.definitionFit: Maps are normally drawn with north at the top, so the extreme on the left is the most occidental point.

clue.text: "Goons" character with a cake from near Manchester

definitions.meaning: a dim-witted figure voiced by Spike Milligan in the BBC radio comedy The Goon Show
a round currant-filled pastry named after a town near Manchester

explanation.surface: A comic radio figure arrives with a bun from the north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goon Show's simpleton shares a name with a Lancashire town whose flaky currant cakes are famous.

clue.text: Permit, utterly, to give a correct mark

indicators.note: utterly is read as in an uttered way, spoken out, so the phrase is heard as it sounds

parts.note: to give something a correct mark is to tick it

explanation.surface: A teacher may, completely, award a right answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like it means 'completely' but means 'when uttered': TICK IT spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass or licence authorising entry or travel.

clue.text: Inflated weapon I cast irresponsibly

parts.note: a bomb is a weapon

indicators.note: acting irresponsibly is behaving wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recklessly launches a blown-up weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflated' sounds like a weapon-related word but describes puffed-up language; 'irresponsibly' is the anagram signal for I CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous, overblown language is puffed up, so the word describes swollen speech.

clue.text: Strength of the pickled pig

definitions.meaning: a cold dish of pork meat from a pig's head, set in jelly or pickled

explanation.surface: A pickled hog's power.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means muscular power and also a jellied pork dish made from a pig's head.

clue.text: Noted art

parts.note: noted looks like famous, but here means written down in notes on a stave, as a composer does

explanation.definitionFit: Melody and harmony are an art form written in notes.

clue.text: Crazy fruit!

explanation.definitionFit: Going bananas is slang for going mad, and the word is also the plural of a yellow tropical fruit.

clue.text: Improved menu that is about food cooked in flour and butter

indicators.note: improved means altered for the better, so these letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A revamped bill of fare that features dishes fried in butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Improved' is the anagram signal for 'menu'; the dish style is French, a la meuniere, from the miller's wife and her flour.
explanation.definitionFit: A la meuniere, in the miller's wife's style, describes fish dredged in flour and fried in butter.

clue.text: Discover knight in a dazed state

indicators.note: in means the knight's letter is placed inside the word for discover

parts.note: to trace is to find or discover
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Someone finds a knight wandering about in a stupor.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-conscious, hypnotic condition.
